questions.q: Why is Status__c on Warranty_Claim__c built as a Picklist instead of free text?
options: Picklists load faster than text fields
Picklists are required on every custom object
Free text fields cannot be added to custom objects
A picklist only accepts predefined valid values, preventing typos and invalid statuses
questions.explain: A picklist restricts entry to a defined list (New/Review/Approved/Denied), which free text cannot enforce.

questions.q: Where does a user go to open any app they have access to?
options: Object Manager
The App Launcher
The Recycle Bin
The Setup Audit Trail
questions.explain: The App Launcher (the grid icon) is where every app a user can open is listed, standard and custom alike.

questions.q: What is the two-click path to creating a new custom object?
options: Object Manager → Create → Custom Object
App Manager → New Lightning App
Setup → Flow Builder → New Flow
App Launcher → Search → New
questions.explain: Object Manager's Create menu, then Custom Object, is the standard starting point for any custom object.

questions.q: Why does this lesson favor the "most declarative solution that satisfies the requirement" over a more impressive custom build?
options: Declarative solutions are always faster to build, with no other benefit
Apex is not allowed on the Salesforce platform
Declarative solutions cannot be tested
Less to maintain, less to break, and easier for the next admin to understand
questions.explain: The lesson explains that minimal, declarative solutions reduce long-term maintenance and hand-off risk — not just build time.

questions.q: Where in Setup do you start building a new custom app?
options: Object Manager
App Manager, via the "New Lightning App" button
The Translation Workbench
Flow Builder
questions.explain: App Manager's "New Lightning App" button launches the four-stage custom app wizard.

questions.q: What happens if a many-to-many relationship gets modeled as a simple one-to-many lookup instead?
options: The data literally can't be captured without duplicating records once both sides need multiple links
Nothing — the two shapes are interchangeable
The object becomes read-only
Reports stop working entirely
questions.explain: A simple lookup can't represent both-sides-multiple relationships — you hit a wall (and likely duplicate data) the first time the real-world data needs that shape.

questions.q: What controls which Global Actions a given user profile actually sees?
options: The Role Hierarchy
The compact layout
The publisher layout
The App Launcher's sort order
questions.explain: The publisher layout determines which global actions are visible to users on a given profile.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what is the single most common mistake with these two tools?
options: Assuming the two tools control the same thing, when they're configured separately and do different jobs
Forgetting to activate a page layout
Using too many compact layouts
Adding too many related lists
questions.explain: The lesson calls out confusing which tool controls what as the single most common Platform App Builder exam mistake.

questions.q: Where do custom Lightning web components appear in the Lightning App Builder?
options: They cannot be used in Lightning App Builder at all
Only inside Object Manager
In the Components panel, alongside standard components, often in a Custom section
Only on the Salesforce mobile app, never on desktop
questions.explain: Custom components show up in the same Components panel as standard ones, typically grouped under a Custom section.

questions.q: Why won't reordering the desktop navigation alone guarantee a tab's position on mobile?
options: Mobile navigation order is set independently via its own Mobile Navigation tab, not inherited automatically from desktop
Desktop and mobile share no configuration at all
Mobile apps cannot display custom tabs
Mobile navigation is fixed and can never be changed
questions.explain: Mobile order is an explicit, separate admin choice — it doesn't automatically mirror whatever order was set for desktop.

questions.q: What does migrating a page to Dynamic Forms actually do?
options: Deletes all fields from the record
Breaks each field and section apart into its own individually placed component on the Lightning App Builder canvas
Converts all fields into a single Apex class
Removes the need for a page layout entirely in every case
questions.explain: Migration turns fields/sections from one page-layout block into individually placed, individually configured components.

questions.q: What has to happen after saving a Lightning page before users can actually see it?
options: Nothing further is needed
Activation — publishing the saved page so it's visible to users
A full sandbox refresh
Rewriting it as a Visualforce page
questions.explain: Saving stores the page, but activation is the separate step that makes it visible to users.

questions.q: What is a junction object?
options: A report that joins two unrelated objects
A custom object with two master-detail relationships, one to each side of a many-to-many relationship
A field that joins text from two other fields
A sandbox used to merge two production orgs
questions.explain: A junction object sits between two objects with a master-detail relationship to each, which is the standard declarative way to model many-to-many relationships.

questions.q: Which of these is something a validation rule CANNOT do?
options: Block a record from being saved
Reference the current and prior value of a changed field
Change or set the value of a field
Display a custom error message at a specific field
questions.explain: A validation rule can only allow or block a save — it has no ability to write or change a field's value. That's a job for a formula field, Flow, or Apex.

questions.q: Which requirement is the best fit for a roll-up summary field?
options: Showing the total value of all open Opportunities on an Account, stored and kept current automatically
Displaying a Case's age in days
Requiring a Close Reason on lost Opportunities
Routing a Contract over $100,000 to a director for sign-off
questions.explain: A stored, automatically-maintained aggregate from direct child records is exactly what a roll-up summary field is built for.

questions.q: What does BLANKVALUE() do in a formula?
options: Substitutes a default value when the referenced field is empty
Deletes a field's value
Converts a number to text
Blocks the record from saving when a field is blank
questions.explain: BLANKVALUE() supplies a fallback when a field is null, which matters because math functions can error on a null instead of silently returning zero.

questions.q: What commonly happens to a record while it is actively in an approval process?
options: It is automatically deleted if not approved within 24 hours
It is locked, preventing further edits until approved, rejected, or recalled
It becomes visible only to System Administrators
Its validation rules are automatically disabled
questions.explain: Initial submission actions typically lock the record, and it stays locked until the process resolves or an admin recalls it.

questions.q: In Salesforce's save order, what happens immediately if a validation rule's formula evaluates to TRUE?
options: The record saves, then a workflow retries the rule
The field is cleared and the save continues
Approval entry criteria are evaluated to see if they override it
The save stops and the error message displays
questions.explain: A TRUE result on a validation rule's formula halts the save at that point and shows the rule's error message to the user.

questions.q: An outbound change set includes a validation rule that references a brand-new custom field, but that field was not added to the change set. What is the practical consequence?
options: Salesforce automatically adds the missing field for you
The deployment will fail or be blocked during validation, because the dependency wasn't included
The validation rule deploys but is automatically deactivated
Nothing — fields and rules deploy completely independently
questions.explain: Change set components can have dependencies; a component that references something not included in the same change set (and not already present in the target org) causes a validation/deployment failure.

questions.q: Why embed a Report Chart or Dashboard component directly on a Lightning app page via Lightning App Builder, instead of leaving it on a separate Reports tab?
options: It is required by Salesforce for all custom objects
It puts the relevant data where the user already is, which is part of what makes an app feel like a finished application rather than a database with a UI
It makes the chart static and unfilterable
It removes the need for any sharing rules on the object
questions.explain: Embedding reports/dashboards directly on the app's own pages means a user doesn't have to go find a separate tab — the current, filtered data is simply there when the app opens.

questions.q: Why does the case study use an approval process (rather than only a validation rule) to handle costly maintenance requests?
options: The requirement is specifically for a named human to review and sign off, with a visible decision and audit trail — exactly what an approval process is built for
Validation rules cannot reference numeric fields like Cost__c
Approval processes are required on every custom object by default
A validation rule would block ALL maintenance requests, not just costly ones
questions.explain: A validation rule can only block or allow a save — it can't route a record to a specific person for review. 'Someone checking it' requires the routing, locking, and audit trail an approval process provides.

questions.q: A user has full record-level sharing access to a record and full field-level security on all its fields, but no object-level access to that object at all. Can they see the record?
options: Yes, because record-level access always overrides object-level access
No — object-level access is the first gate, and a gap there blocks the user regardless of the other layers
Yes, but only in Salesforce Classic
Only if they are a System Administrator
questions.explain: Security layers are not forgiving-additive: the user needs object access AND field access AND record access. A missing object-level grant blocks access even with everything else wide open.

questions.q: What rollout approach does this lesson recommend over flipping a switch for everyone at once?
options: Deploying directly to production with no sandbox testing
Disabling the app for managers until all reps have used it
Phasing the rollout by assigning the new app's permission set to a pilot group first, gathering feedback, then expanding
Skipping training entirely and relying on in-app guidance alone
questions.explain: A phased rollout by permission set lets a pilot group surface real problems before the whole organization is exposed to them.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what Flow capability did the Help Desk Ticket capstone deliberately NOT use, leaving it for the next course in the path?
options: Formula fields
Record-triggered Flow, loops, collections, subflows, and scheduled processing
Validation rules
Change sets
questions.explain: The capstone used only a short screen Flow triggering an approval. Deeper Flow capabilities — record-triggered automation, loops, collections, subflows, scheduling — are explicitly left for the Flow Automation course that follows.
